key_insight: SWE-Serve is a benchmark that measures whether agents can make production-correct inference serving changes across an entire repository, not just solve isolated coding tasks.
engineering_relevance: It is relevant because production inference engineering requires coordinated edits to models, runtimes, and APIs, making local task success insufficient for real deployment quality.
method: 53 repository-grounded tasks from recent SGLang production changes
Covers six inference engineering families and runs on CPU or a single H100 GPU
Uses hidden functional/regression tests, optional E2E serving tests, and calibrated performance gates
evidence_signal: Across 11 models and 31 model-effort settings, the best configuration reached 75% mean pass@1, while on 19 E2E-covered tasks the serving tests rejected about one-third of patches that otherwise passed.
watch_item: Results may depend on the benchmark’s SGLang-derived task mix and hidden test design, so generalization to other serving stacks or production environments should be validated carefully.
paper_title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
